title: A Monitoring-Harness Prototype: Streaming Safety Flags Over Agent Trajectories

original_idea.body:
# A Monitoring-Harness Prototype: Streaming Safety Flags Over Agent Trajectories

**Problem:** A success state requires lightweight runtime monitors that flag unsafe agent steps as they happen. A needed result is a small, open, reusable monitoring-harness prototype that beginners can extend.

**Direction:** Build a thin wrapper around a simple open-model agent loop that, at each step, runs a fast judge to emit a per-step risk score (tool-misuse, scope-violation, goal-drift) and logs a trajectory timeline. Validate on a handful of scripted safe/unsafe trajectories. Deliverable: an open monitoring-harness prototype plus a worked detection demo.

**Why it matters:** Safer monitoring harnesses are exactly the strategically valuable infrastructure the steering prioritizes, and labs build proprietary versions. A small open prototype seeds community tooling, needs only a consumer GPU, and targets agentic deployment safety.

**Relevant context:** AMDM live monitoring (Shukla 2025) cross-normalizes harm-rate/goal-drift; Inspect AI (UK AISI) and AISafetyLab provide extensible eval scaffolds (context file, source code availability); OWASP Top 10 Agentic (2025) on tool misuse/goal hijack.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (runtime monitoring infrastructure aids agentic safety) but a prototype's validation-on-scripted-trajectories is a gap to demonstrated impact.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Thin wrapper + per-step judge + logging; guidable engineering for novice+mentor.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (prototype + demo) but building the harness + judge + scripted trajectories has a few parts.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open monitoring infrastructure labs build proprietarily; seeds community tooling - strategically valuable.

low_compute.reasoning: Open-model agent loop + judge, consumer GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Agent-monitoring harnesses exist (AMDM, Inspect AI); a prototype is largely re-building known tooling.
